no_elections_reason: The Taliban's Islamic Emirate held no elections in 1996-2001 and has held none since it returned to power on 15 August 2021. The elections of the Interim and Transitional Administrations and the Islamic Republic (2002-2019) are recorded below; the Islamic Republic's five-year presidential and Wolesi Jirga terms ended with its fall.

historical.note: The Emergency Loya Jirga (Kabul, 11-19 June 2002) elected the head of the Transitional Administration by secret ballot on 13 June; Karzai won about 83%. The two other candidates, Masooda Jalal and Mahfoz Nadai, are not stored. Karzai was sworn in on 19 June.
Eighteen candidates; Karzai won in the first round. Mohaqiq and Dostum are listed as independents backed by their parties.

source.title: Wikipedia: 2004 Afghan presidential election (infobox and results table)

historical.note: All candidates stood as individuals under single non-transferable vote (official result: 249 independents). Seats by party are the Wikipedia affiliation table. 'Others' are Hezbe Eqtedar Milli 12, Hezb-e Islami (registered party) 12, National United Party 8, Afghan Mellat 8, National Islamic Front 3, Islamic Movement 3, National Solidarity Movement 3 and National Solidarity Party 1. Turnout was estimated at 50%.

source.title: Wikipedia: 2005 Afghan parliamentary election (infobox and affiliation table)

historical.note: Certified final result of 21 October 2009: 4,597,727 valid votes after the Electoral Complaints Commission invalidated about 1.07 million ballots. No candidate reached 50%; the run-off was not held because Abdullah withdrew, and Karzai was declared the winner. Abdullah's party label is omitted (the National Coalition was founded in 2010).

source.title: Wikipedia: 2009 Afghan presidential election (infobox and results table)

historical.review_note: The fetched excerpts confirm the certified totals but not the exact date Karzai was declared the winner after Abdullah's withdrawal (early November 2009); add it to the note.

historical.note: Official result: 249 seats won by individual candidates (239 general and 10 Kuchi seats). Seats by party follow the Wikipedia affiliation table; 'others' (Jamhori 9, National Islamic Front 6, Afghan Mellat 4, National Solidarity Party 4, Islamic Movement 4 and nine parties with 1 each) and 'independents' (the remainder, 164) are derived from it. Turnout was about 3.6 million of more than 10 million eligible voters.

source.title: Wikipedia: 2010 Afghan parliamentary election (infobox and affiliation table)

historical.note: First round 5 April, second round 14 June 2014. After a UN-supervised audit the second-round valid votes fell from 7,972,727 to 7,120,585; the Independent Election Commission announced Ghani as the winner on 19 September 2014. Karzai could not stand because of term limits.

source.title: Wikipedia: 2014 Afghan presidential election (infobox and results table)

historical.note: Voting took place on 20 and 27 October 2018. All 244 filled seats (233 general, 10 Kuchi, 1 Sikh and Hindu) went to candidates standing as individuals; 6 seats stayed vacant. No party breakdown is given by the source, so no winning party is recorded.
Fourteen candidates; registered electorate 9,665,745. Ghani won in the first round. Abdullah rejected the result and announced a parallel government.
